$comment: 20 Strategy Tester scenarios per dispatch §4.2 / phase_1_build_intent.md §5.2 + OPEN-001 floor-fix dispatch (s13-s17) + OPEN-001 daily-anchor correction (s18-s19) + FIX 2b daily-DD basis/mandatory-reset correction (s18-s19 rewritten, s20 added). FIX 2b: daily DD now RESETS every EET trading day (mandatory, both bases) and Daily_DD_Basis selects only the denominator (INITIAL=fixed % of initial floor / DAY_START=% of day-start equity); the FIX 2 static-non-resetting daily anchor was a bug (froze accounts permanently once ~3.5% below initial). s18 = reset+basis observable; s19 = restart re-snapshot; s20 = fires-then-clears-at-rollover regression guard. Schema 1.3 reflects Option 1 + Bug A fix: exit reason vocabulary replaced opaque 'broker_closed' with strategic reasons {trail_stop, initial_sl_hit, equity_guard_force, external_close, time_exit}, and broker-side exit rows now carry actual fill_price via deal-history lookup. schema 1.2 re-validated dates under canonical R (1R = sl_distance_price = sl_atr_mult × ATR per core/sim/exit_policies/_base.py:95) after the r_atr fix in commit 164ffb5. historical_signal_bar_close carries the verified date for price-driven scenarios — picked by scanning HistData M1 for real-market sequences that produce each scenario's expected play. s13-s17 verify the OPEN-001 fix: Total-DD floor is solely operator-set (Initial_Equity_Floor input), static, never captured from live equity; observable is the '[ARC10] equity init: floor=… source=…' journal line. Schema structure unchanged from 1.3 (new scenarios reuse existing fields + ea_input_overrides).

scenarios.title: Entry → trail → trail SL exit
scenarios.narrative: Bar N+1 fills near 1.0842. Price rallies to >+1R triggering partial close (50%). Peak ratchets across subsequent H4 bars; trail SL = peak - 1R follows. Eventually a bar closes below trail; EA queues full close of remaining 50% at next-bar open.
scenarios.setup_note: POST_R_FIX_SANITY_CHECK: re-run this scenario first after EA recompile. Under canonical R, TP1 level = entry + sl_distance = entry + 0.00749 (vs prior buggy +0.00214). Whether the 2026-03-10 EURUSD entry bar reaches the wider TP1 determines whether s1 still partials (then trails) or becomes a straight-SL outcome. Different result vs prior s1 run is EXPECTED and CORRECT — the prior s1 'pass' was against the buggy EA. The Python sim's WFO was validated under canonical R; this is the baseline that matters.

scenarios.title: Entry → SL hit (no partial)
scenarios.narrative: Bar N+1 fills near 1.2540. Price drops directly to -1R before any +1R cross. Broker SL fires; EA's intra-tick TP1 check never fires; bar_ordinal updates do nothing for trail. exit fires at broker fill.
scenarios.setup_note: Re-scanned under canonical R. Entry fill (open 2026-04-02 00:00Z H4 bar) = 1.33054. SL @ 1.31829 (entry - 0.01225); TP1 @ 1.34279 (entry + 0.01225 = canonical +1R, NOT +0.00350). Forward 4 H4 bars: highs 1.33200/1.32481/1.32256/1.32483 (TP1 never touched), bar 4 (2026-04-02T12:00) low 1.31815 ≤ SL → broker_closed.

scenarios.title: Entry → partial → BE-equivalent trail SL hit (zero net R)
scenarios.narrative: TP1 fires; trail activates at peak - 1R. Peak doesn't extend (small post-TP1 reversal). Bar closes back at entry-equivalent (peak = entry+R, trail = entry). Full close at next bar open. Net R = 0.5 (partial captured) + 0 (runner) = 0.25 in lot-weighted terms.
scenarios.setup_note: Re-scanned under canonical R. Entry fill = 0.62862. TP1 @ 0.63282 (= entry + 0.00420). TP1 fires on bar 3 (2025-03-12T20:00, high = 0.63282 exactly). Peak ratchets to 0.63334 on next bar; trail level = 0.62914. Exit bar 2025-03-13T08:00 close 0.62863 ≤ trail → exits ~1 pip above entry (near-BE on runner). Net P&L = +0.5R partial.

scenarios.title: Entry → partial → big runner with multiple ratchets → exit
scenarios.narrative: TP1 fires. Over 8-15 bars, peak high ratchets up steadily; trail SL ratchets up each bar via PositionModify. Eventually a bar closes below the highest trail level; runner exits.
scenarios.setup_note: Re-scanned under canonical R. ONLY 7 candidates in 2020-2026 meet spec (8-18 bars, ≥3 new highs, peak-entry ≥5 yen). No 2024+ alternative — post-2024 USDJPY ranges don't produce 5+ yen multi-bar runners at the synthetic 0.40 ATR / 1.40 sl_distance. PRIMARY is COVID-era yen-carry unwind: entry 105.843 (2020-03-17 00:00Z fill). TP1 @ 107.243 fires bar 1 (high 107.592). Peak ratchets through 9 new highs → 111.361 by 2020-03-19T20:00. Exit 2020-03-20T04:00 close 109.507 ≤ trail 109.961 → runner exits +3.66 yen above entry. Net captured ≈ 5.5 yen. ⚠ MT5 may need history-extended to load March 2020 H4 — Tools > Options > Charts > 'Max bars in chart' ≥ 100000.

scenarios.title: Entry → partial → time exit at bar 240
scenarios.narrative: TP1 fires. Price drifts sideways for 240 H4 bars without trail-stopping. bar_ordinal reaches 240; time exit queued; close at next bar open.
scenarios.setup_note: TIME_EXIT_BARS_OVERRIDE: 12 — 240-bar quiet windows are unachievable in NZDUSD 2020-2026 EVEN UNDER CANONICAL R (3.5× wider trail). Re-scan post-r_atr fix confirms: 4,121 TP1 entries evaluated; longest post-TP1 quiet run is 77 H4 bars (2025-11-26 cluster); zero runs ≥ 80 bars. Time-exit mechanic tested at 12-bar override — this is a data-driven limitation, not a residue of the prior R bug. PRIMARY entry fill ≈ 0.56245 (2025-11-26 04:00Z open); TP1 fires within first few bars; should survive well past 12 bars under canonical R trail before time-exit closes the runner at bar 12 open.

scenarios.title: News block at signal time
scenarios.narrative: Calendar contains a high-impact USD or EUR event within ±300s of entry_bar_open_utc (FIX 3 widened the window from ±120s to ±5min). EA delays entry until event_time + 305s (News_Window_Sec + News_Delay_Buffer_Sec). If delay would push past signal+1h, signal is discarded. This scenario sets up the delay case; news event fires before entry, then entry fires at delay_to.
scenarios.setup_note: REQUIRES_UPCOMING_NFP: FF calendar (https://nfs.faireconomy.media) only carries current+next ~2 weeks of events; historical replay not possible. To run: pick an upcoming NFP date (first Friday, 12:30 or 13:30 UTC depending on DST), set --signal-bar-close to that exact timestamp, enable WebRequest for nfs.faireconomy.media in MT5 Tools > Options > Expert Advisors. If no NFP falls in your test window, defer s6 to live deployment.

scenarios.title: Equity guard block at signal time
scenarios.narrative: Account equity has drawn down to ≥3.5% from EET day open (Daily_DD_Halt_Pct). EA's equity-guard rejects entry; signal moves to signals_failed/ with reason=daily_dd_halt.
scenarios.setup_note: FORCE_TRIGGER_OVERRIDE: Daily_DD_Halt_Pct lowered to 0.00001 (effectively zero) so any floating P&L on the first tick triggers the guard. Real 3.5% DD setup would require staging a prior losing trade on a different pair before the s7 envelope — not worth the complexity for a logging-only verification.

scenarios.title: Same-bar dual-touch event (log only)
scenarios.narrative: A single H4 bar contains both bar.high >= entry+1R (TP1 trigger) AND bar.low <= entry-1R (would-have-been SL). EA fires partial intra-tick first (Bid touches +1R before SL); SL then fires later in the same bar on the broker. Phase 2 will measure the R impact vs Python convention.
scenarios.setup_note: NO_HISTORICAL_CANDIDATE: post-r_atr-fix re-scan confirms ZERO historical bars in 6+ years (2020-2026) of GBPJPY data where a single H4 bar straddles BOTH entry+sl_distance (=+2.80) AND entry-sl_distance (=-2.80) from a valid entry-bar open. The widest H4 bars (top 5 reach 5.4-6.8 yen range, e.g. 2022-09-26 BoJ intervention 6.79 yen, 2024-08-05 yen-carry unwind 5.68 yen) ALL gap past their entries rather than straddling — the entry-bar open lands outside the 5.60-wide central band. Genuine same-bar 2-sided ±2.80 events from-entry do not occur in the historical record. Options: (a) skip s8 — runtime gracefully handles the no-s8-event case; (b) test with synthetic data (manufacture a Custom Symbol bar in MT5 that produces the dual-touch); (c) defer Phase 2 same-bar precedence verification to code inspection. The prior schema-1.1 use of 2022-09-22 BoJ day was based on the BUGGY R (+1×ATR threshold easier to hit) — invalid under canonical R.

scenarios.title: EA restart mid-trade, pre-partial
scenarios.narrative: Place entry; restart EA via Strategy Tester restart hook. On reinit, RecoveryManager enumerates broker positions filtered by magic, reconstructs entry_bar_time, peak_high_bid from H4 bars, finds no partial in deal history → tp1_fired=false. Continues management normally.
scenarios.setup_note: PAIR_SUBSTITUTION_USDJPY: spec'd USDCAD substituted with USDJPY 2020-03-16T20:00:00Z (= new s4 candidate post-r_atr-fix) because USDCAD wasn't verified in the historical scan and the recovery logic is pair-agnostic. Procedure: start tester; when [ARC10] entry appears in journal, immediately edit any EA input (forces restart) BEFORE [ARC10] PARTIAL TP1 fired; observe [ARC10] recovered USDJPY ... tp1=no in journal and recovery_reconstructed row in trade_log.csv. ⚠ Same MT5 history-extension note as s4 (March 2020 H4 bars must be loaded).

scenarios.title: EA restart mid-trade, post-partial
scenarios.narrative: Place entry, TP1 fires, restart. On reinit, deal history shows a partial-close deal with volume < initial; reconstruct tp1_fired=true, partial_close_price=<deal price>, peak_high_bid from H4 highs. Trail level may need broker SL ratchet. Continues management.
scenarios.setup_note: PAIR_SUBSTITUTION_USDJPY: same as s9. Procedure: start tester; wait for [ARC10] PARTIAL TP1 fired (bar 1 of s4 setup, ~107.59); force restart; observe recovery row in trade_log.csv with note=tp1=yes.

scenarios.title: Sidecar stale heartbeat (existing positions managed; new entries blocked)
scenarios.narrative: Active position exists. ea.heartbeat is fresh but sidecar.heartbeat is older than Sidecar_Heartbeat_Max_Age_Sec. EA ArcPollSignals() and news refresh are skipped this tick; existing position management continues (TP1, trail, time exit). New synthetic signal dropped into signals_out/ is NOT picked up while heartbeat stale.
scenarios.setup_note: STALE_HEARTBEAT_OVERRIDE: write sidecar.heartbeat with last_heartbeat_utc="2026-03-09T00:00:00Z" (= 32 sim-hours BEFORE signal, well past 600s threshold). Verify in journal: [ARC10] sidecar-heartbeat stale=true at sim_utc=... at OnInit and never flips to stale=false; no [ARC10] poll: lines appear; trade_log.csv empty.

scenarios.title: Invalid config_hash (signal rejected)
scenarios.narrative: Fake_sidecar emits with config_hash that doesn't match Expected_Config_Hash. EA's ArcSignalParse returns config_hash_mismatch; signal moves to signals_failed/. No order placed.
scenarios.setup_note: BAD_HASH_OVERRIDE: pass --config-hash "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111" (or any 64-char value != EA's Expected_Config_Hash). Verify in journal: [ARC10] signal parse failed EURUSD_...: config_hash_mismatch and envelope moved to signals_failed\.

scenarios.title: Floor input set, EA restarted — floor unchanged after restart
scenarios.narrative: Operator sets Initial_Equity_Floor=100000. EA inits; journal shows floor=100000.00 source=input. EA is restarted via input-edit (forces OnInit, same trigger as s9/s10). After restart the floor is re-read from the input and is still 100000.00 source=input — it is NOT recaptured from live equity, so it is independent of MT5 profile-persistence.
scenarios.setup_note: FLOOR_RESTART: set Initial_Equity_Floor=100000 in the EA inputs. Start tester; verify journal '[ARC10] equity init: floor=100000.00 source=input'. While running, edit any OTHER EA input (e.g. a whitespace-neutral toggle) to force a restart per the s9/s10 input-edit procedure; verify the post-restart init line again reads floor=100000.00 source=input. PASS = floor value identical across both inits and source=input both times. No trade events expected (logging/observable-only verification).

scenarios.title: Floor=100000, equity below floor, restart — floor still 100000 (bug case)
scenarios.narrative: The original-bug case. Initial_Equity_Floor=100000 while live equity sits below the floor (target ~94000). EA is restarted. Under the old code the floor would be re-snapshotted from live equity (94000), permanently lowering the total-DD anchor. Under the fix the floor is re-read from the input and stays 100000.00 source=input — the floor is decoupled from live equity entirely.
scenarios.setup_note: FLOOR_VS_EQUITY_DECOUPLE: set Initial_Equity_Floor=100000. Driving ST equity to a precise 94000 requires staging prior losing trades and is impractical in the tester — but it is NOT required to prove the fix: because the floor is sourced from the input (source=input) and never from AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_EQUITY), the post-restart floor is provably independent of whatever equity is. PASS = post-restart journal reads floor=100000.00 source=input (NOT a live-equity value). If the operator does want the literal sub-floor-equity condition, stage a losing position on another pair before restart and confirm the init line still prints floor=100000.00 source=input despite equity < 100000.

scenarios.title: Floor input changed 100000 → 125000 — manual scale-up path
scenarios.narrative: Manual scale-up: the operator raises Initial_Equity_Floor from 100000 to 125000 (e.g. after a 5ers scale-up) and restarts the EA. The new floor is adopted from the input: journal reads floor=125000.00 source=input. Scale-up is purely an operator input edit — there is no scale-up state struct, JSON state file, or live capture.
scenarios.setup_note: FLOOR_SCALE_UP: run once with Initial_Equity_Floor=100000 (verify floor=100000.00 source=input), then change the input to 125000 and restart. PASS = post-change journal reads floor=125000.00 source=input. Demonstrates the only supported scale-up mechanism is editing the operator input.

scenarios.title: Floor=125000, equity below floor, restart — floor still 125000
scenarios.narrative: Post-scale-up variant of s14. Initial_Equity_Floor=125000 while live equity sits below it (target ~120000). After restart the floor is re-read from the input and stays 125000.00 source=input — never recaptured to 120000. Confirms the decoupling holds at the scaled-up anchor too.
scenarios.setup_note: FLOOR_VS_EQUITY_DECOUPLE_SCALED: identical procedure to s14 at the scaled-up value. set Initial_Equity_Floor=125000; restart. PASS = post-restart journal reads floor=125000.00 source=input (NOT a live-equity value such as 120000). The floor's independence from live equity is what the fix guarantees.

scenarios.title: Floor input = 0 — EA refuses to trade, fires Alert, journals sentinel-fail
scenarios.narrative: Fail-loud path. Initial_Equity_Floor is left at its default 0 (unset). On OnInit the EA detects the implausible floor (< 1000), sets g_arc_eq_floor_fail, fires Alert('[ARC10] FLOOR UNSET — EA halted, set Initial_Equity_Floor'), journals an ERROR FLOOR_FAIL line plus 'floor=0.00 source=sentinel-fail', and refuses all entries. A dropped signal envelope is rejected at the equity gate with reason floor_unset_halt and logged as an equity_block row. The EA's ea.heartbeat carries status=halted_floor_unset for the always-up sidecar to detect.
scenarios.setup_note: FLOOR_UNSET_FAILLOUD: leave Initial_Equity_Floor=0 (default). Start tester. PASS requires ALL of: (1) Alert popup '[ARC10] FLOOR UNSET — EA halted, set Initial_Equity_Floor'; (2) journal '[ARC10] ERROR FLOOR_FAIL: Initial_Equity_Floor=0.00 implausible ...'; (3) journal '[ARC10] equity init: floor=0.00 source=sentinel-fail'; (4) ea.heartbeat JSON contains "status": "halted_floor_unset"; (5) staging the s7-style envelope yields an equity_block row in trade_log.csv with reason floor_unset_halt and the signal moved to signals_failed\ — NO entry/order is placed.

scenarios.title: Daily-DD resets at EET rollover; basis selects denominator (FIX 2b)
scenarios.narrative: Verifies the daily-DD reset + basis after FIX 2b (supersedes the FIX 2 static-anchor behaviour s18 used to assert). The daily-DD measurement is a day-start EQUITY snapshot that RESETS every EET trading day — mandatory, both bases. At OnInit the EA logs '[ARC10] daily-DD basis=INITIAL reset=daily' (the basis+reset proof line) and '[ARC10] daily day-start: equity=… source=init-snapshot'. At each EET-day rollover (00:00 EET = 22:00 UTC winter / 21:00 UTC summer) it logs '[ARC10] eet-rollover: daily-DD reset day_start_equity=… basis=INITIAL …', RE-SNAPSHOTTING the day-start equity to the current equity and clearing the per-day entry-halt flag. daily_dd = (day_start_equity - equity) / denom, where denom = Initial_Equity_Floor for INITIAL (fixed $/day — 4.5% = $4,500) or this day's start equity for DAY_START. The TOTAL-DD floor is separate, static, and unaffected ('floor=100000.00 source=input' throughout).
scenarios.setup_note: DAILY_RESET_AND_BASIS: set Initial_Equity_Floor=100000, Daily_DD_Basis=INITIAL (default). Run across ≥2 EET days. PASS = (a) exactly ONE '[ARC10] daily-DD basis=INITIAL reset=daily' line + ONE 'daily day-start: equity=… source=init-snapshot' at start; (b) one '[ARC10] eet-rollover: daily-DD reset day_start_equity=… basis=INITIAL …' line per EET boundary crossed, each re-snapshotting day_start_equity to that day's current equity (the value tracks equity at rollover, it does NOT stay pinned to 100000); (c) the TOTAL floor line 'floor=100000.00 source=input' is unchanged across the whole run. Optional: re-run with Daily_DD_Basis=DAY_START and confirm the basis token flips to DAY_START in both the attach and rollover lines. Observable-only; no trade events required.

scenarios.title: Mid-day restart re-snapshots the daily day-start to current equity (FIX 2b)
scenarios.narrative: Verifies the restart behaviour of the daily day-start after FIX 2b. A mid-day EA restart (OnInit re-fire via input-edit, same trigger as s9/s10) re-snapshots the daily day-start to the CURRENT equity (source=init-snapshot) — it is NOT persisted to a state file and NOT the static floor. Daily risk is bounded to one day by the natural rollover, so a fresh snapshot on restart is correct. The basis line '[ARC10] daily-DD basis=INITIAL reset=daily' prints again. The TOTAL floor is independently re-read from the operator input (s13/s14) and stays 100000.00 source=input — total and daily are separate (total never resets; daily resets at rollover and re-snapshots on restart).
scenarios.setup_note: DAILY_RESTART_RESNAPSHOT: set Initial_Equity_Floor=100000. Start tester; note the first 'daily day-start: equity=… source=init-snapshot' and 'daily-DD basis=INITIAL reset=daily'. While running and BEFORE any EET rollover, edit any EA input to force a restart (s9/s10 input-edit procedure). PASS = a SECOND 'source=init-snapshot' line printing the restart-time CURRENT equity (re-snapshot, not the static floor, not a persisted prior value), and the basis line re-printed. The TOTAL floor line reads 'floor=100000.00 source=input' both times (total-floor logic untouched).

scenarios.title: Daily governor fires then CLEARS at rollover — no permanent freeze (FIX 2b)
scenarios.narrative: The FIX 2b regression guard. Under the FIX 2 bug, daily DD was anchored to the static floor and never reset, so once equity sat ~3.5% below initial the daily governors fired on every bar PERMANENTLY and froze the account — not a daily limit. After FIX 2b, the daily measurement resets at EET rollover: a day that hits the 3.5% halt clears at the next EET day, and because day-start equity re-snapshots to the (lower) current equity, daily_dd restarts near zero and entries resume — even while the account is still down from initial. Demonstrated: day 1 a forced daily halt blocks a signal (equity_block, reason=daily_dd_halt); at the EET rollover the EA logs 'eet-rollover: daily-DD reset day_start_equity=…' and clears the entry-halt flag; day 2 a fresh signal is ACCEPTED (entry). The total-DD halt (static floor, 7/8%) is untouched and would still hold if a real total breach existed.
scenarios.setup_note: DAILY_CLEAR_AT_ROLLOVER: set Initial_Equity_Floor=100000, Daily_DD_Halt_Pct=0.00001 (so any floating loss on day 1 trips the daily halt, like s7), Daily_DD_CloseAll_Pct at its 0.045 default. Stage a day-1 signal envelope at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z (within EET day 2026-03-10) plus a tiny floating loss → day-1 signal is rejected at the equity gate with reason=daily_dd_halt (equity_block row). Run past the next EET rollover (22:00 UTC 2026-03-10 → EET day 2026-03-11); confirm the journal shows '[ARC10] eet-rollover: daily-DD reset day_start_equity=… basis=INITIAL …' AND that g_arc_eq_entries_halted_today has cleared. Stage a day-2 signal (e.g. 2026-03-11T08:00:00Z); with the day-2 floating P&L flat-or-positive at that tick it is ACCEPTED → entry row. PASS = day-1 equity_block(daily_dd_halt) → rollover-reset line → day-2 entry (account did NOT freeze). Contrast: under the FIX 2 bug the day-2 signal would also be blocked indefinitely. (If staging precise floating losses in ST is impractical, the regression is equivalently provable by inspecting the rollover line: day_start_equity re-snapshots to current equity each day and the halt flag clears — code path in ArcEquityOnTick.)
